title: 'Flock Flocked up'

reading.body:
This is a case of a system acting on a misread input and a human chain treating that output as established fact. The failure sits at the front of the deployment, where an automated licence plate reader generated a match that did not exist, and everything after it, the stop, the drawn guns, the dog, the charges, followed from that single false flag. The camera read a plate belonging to a Chevy Malibu as being on a red Dodge Ram pickup, a mismatch between vehicle type and plate that was present in the system's own output.

Catching it would have required a check at the point of dispatch or before the stop, comparing the flagged vehicle description against what the camera actually captured. The reporting indicates officers only learned the plate information was wrong after the arrest, and that an officer said on camera the system likely misread the plate. Nothing in the facts shows a verification step existed between the camera's alert and the armed stop.

What is not established is how the misread occurred, whether the system had a known error rate, or whether anyone reviewed the alert before officers acted. The department's investigation found no wrongdoing in the use of the K-9, and charges were later dropped according to the driver's lawyer, but the reports do not establish intent, fault, or what consequence followed for the camera system itself.

reports.title: Body cam of TPD officers releasing K-9 on man during traffic stop
Man speaks out after police release K-9 on him during traffic stop: 'Traumatized'
TPD investigation finds no wrongdoing in use of K-9 on man during traffic stop
Charges dropped against man Toledo Police released K-9 on during traffic stop, lawyer says

summary:
Toledo Police released body camera video showing officers using a K-9 on a driver during a traffic stop. The stop began after a FLOCK camera wrongly flagged a stolen license plate. The camera image belonged to a Chevy Malibu, but the plate was seen on a red Dodge Ram pickup. Officers stopped the truck with guns drawn and told driver Brandon Upchurch to get out. He raised his hands and asked why he was stopped, then walked onto the grass. The K-9 handler moved closer with the dog, and Upchurch was arrested and charged with resisting arrest and obstruction.

Officers later learned the plate information was wrong and the truck did not have the stolen plate. An officer said on camera that the system likely misread the plate. Upchurch received medical attention at the scene. Police said they believed he might flee and did not know if he or a passenger had weapons. The article does not say what happens next.
